paras: Canberra gardens run on a sharp calendar, and any gardener Canberra wide works to it. Hard frosts from May to August mean frost-tender plants are pruned in spring, while roses and deciduous shrubs are pruned in winter. From September everything grows at once, and weeds arrive in the beds with the spring bulbs.

Summers are hot and dry, so mulching in late spring is one of the most useful things a gardener Canberra wide can do for a bed, holding moisture and keeping roots cool with water restrictions in mind. Autumn brings leaf drop from the deciduous street trees in Deakin and Chapman, and a clean-up before winter keeps gutters, paths and beds clear.
